title: Only 8% Pass This Paramedic Entrance Exam
summary: Scene hazards, vital signs and rapid-response decisions test whether you can think clearly when every clue matters.

landing.intro: From scene hazards and vital signs to emergency maths and calm communication, prove you can think clearly when every clue matters.

questions.question: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
A call is logged at 14:35. The crew reaches the destination at 15:12. How much time has passed?

visual.ariaLabel: Call logged at 14:35 and arrival at 15:12

questions.question: How should the floor hazard be handled first?

visual.ariaLabel: Used sharp, broken glass and a clear exit

answers: Isolate the hazard and report it
Move it carefully with a gloved hand
Slide it away from the walkway with your shoe
Leave it until the scene is quieter

questions.question: Which measurement changed?

visual.ariaLabel: Pulse unchanged, breathing increased, alertness unchanged, skin warmth unchanged

questions.question: Which opening makes the clearest handover?
answers: Here are all the minor details in random order
At 14:20, breathing became faster and alertness decreased
I already know exactly what caused it

questions.question: Which takes priority?
questions.context: A routine equipment checklist is due soon. At the same time, a person who was comfortable becomes pale, dizzy and less responsive.
answers: Prioritise the person’s sudden deterioration and seek qualified help
Complete the routine checklist before responding
Wait until the checklist deadline has passed
Choose whichever task is physically nearest

questions.question: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
Four sealed packs hold five dressings each. How many dressings are there?
Which chamber receives oxygen-rich blood returning from the lungs?

visual.ariaLabel: Oxygen-rich blood travels from the lungs through an unknown chamber before the left ventricle

questions.question: Which body system carries signals between the brain and the rest of the body?
Which statement best describes the kidneys?
answers: They exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide
They remove wastes from blood and help regulate water balance

questions.question: Which body-function detail changed?
questions.context: Earlier, both hand grips were equal. Now the right grip is unchanged, but the left grip is weaker than before.

questions.question: Which newly recorded change matters most?
questions.context: Earlier the person was alert and answered promptly. Now they are drowsy and respond much more slowly.
answers: The time written on the card

questions.question: What is the best interpretation of this pattern?

visual.ariaLabel: Pulse 80 then 92 then 108, with pallor and dizziness

answers: The combined trend suggests deterioration needing prompt qualified assessment
The symptoms can be ignored because no diagnosis is shown

questions.question: Why can reduced breathing affect working tissues?
answers: Less oxygen can enter the blood and reach the tissues
The kidneys stop receiving nerve signals

questions.question: Which change is the strongest warning of deterioration?
A live electrical cable lies across the only doorway. What comes first?
answers: Keep everyone clear and get qualified help to make it safe
Move it with a dry object
Ask a bystander to watch it

questions.question: A person is beside moving traffic with no protected working area. What is safest?
answers: Keep clear, identify the danger and seek appropriate scene support
Walk into traffic and wave vehicles around
Ask the person to cross the road immediately
Place equipment in the road to slow vehicles

questions.question: A task may expose the face and hands to splashing body fluid. What guides PPE choice?
answers: The colour of the equipment bag
The assessed exposure risk, including hand and eye or face protection

questions.question: A coughing person is sharing a small waiting area. Which general safety action fits the visible risk?
answers: Turn off all ventilation without assessment
Encourage respiratory and hand hygiene and follow risk-based precautions

questions.question: Which detail is most urgent to hand over?

visual.ariaLabel: Vehicle stopped, two people, strong fuel smell

answers: The fuel smell and possible ignition hazard

questions.question: A person keeps nodding but has not understood. What should happen next?
answers: Repeat the same answer review more slowly
Ask, ‘Do you understand?’ and continue if they say yes
Shorten the answer review but keep the same terminology
Use plain words and check back

questions.question: A bystander starts discussing a person's private details where others can hear. What is best?
answers: Move the conversation to a private setting and share only necessary information
Repeat the details so everyone understands
Post the information on a public notice

questions.question: Someone needs to discuss a sensitive health concern. What protects dignity?
answers: Ask them to explain in front of everyone
Find a private setting and listen without making assumptions
Tell nearby people the concern first

questions.question: A person says, “I'm terrified.” Which response is best?
answers: There is nothing to be scared about
Try not to think about it
I guarantee everything will be fine
I can see this is frightening. Tell me what worries you most

questions.question: Which response protects privacy and checks understanding?
questions.context: The person says, “I do not want this discussed where others can hear, and I still do not understand why you are asking.”
answers: Continue the discussion where everyone can hear
Avoid explaining and ask the same questions again
Move to an appropriate private setting, explain plainly and check understanding
Ask a bystander to explain on your behalf

questions.question: Which concern has the highest priority?
questions.context: The person's chest is moving, but very little air movement can be detected and they cannot speak normally.
answers: A possible airway or breathing problem needing immediate qualified assessment

questions.question: Who needs attention first?
questions.context: Person A feels well and their observations remain steady. Person B is newly clammy and dizzy, and their pulse has risen across three checks.
answers: Person B, because several changes point to deterioration
Person A, because their observations were recorded first
Both can wait because neither has a named diagnosis
The person with the shorter name

questions.question: Which new information should change the response most?
questions.context: The scene was initially reported as safe. A second update says smoke is now entering the room and the nearest exit is becoming difficult to use.
answers: The original report that the scene was safe
The developing smoke and threatened exit route
The time the first report was written
The number of words in the update

questions.question: Which first radio message gives responders the clearest immediate picture?

visual.ariaLabel: Only one urgent message can be sent first and radio time is limited

answers: We need help somewhere near the road
River Gate: two people, smoke present, access blocked
The scene is difficult; more details will follow
Please arrive quickly; equipment may be needed

questions.question: What is the combined recorded volume in millilitres?

visual.ariaLabel: 0.3 litres plus 450 millilitres plus 250 millilitres equals what total

questions.question: A 500 mL record is 70% complete. How many millilitres have been recorded?
Who needs attention first?

items: PERSON A::Sore wrist · normal speech · steady observations
PERSON B::Collapsed · pale · rapid breathing · new confusion
visual.ariaLabel: Person A has a sore wrist, normal speech and steady observations. Person B collapsed and is pale, breathing rapidly and newly confused.

questions.question: If shallow breathing reduces gas exchange, what downstream effect follows most directly?

items: SHALLOW BREATHING → LESS GAS EXCHANGE → ? → LESS OXYGEN TO TISSUES
visual.ariaLabel: Shallow breathing, less gas exchange, unknown, less oxygen to tissues

questions.question: What is the best interpretation of the complete trend?

visual.ariaLabel: Breathing 16 alert, then 22 anxious, then 28 drowsy

answers: The values can be ignored because no diagnosis is named
Breathing is worsening while responsiveness is declining

questions.question: A 1.2 L total is divided equally across four recorded periods. How much belongs to each period?
What is the safest response to the combined hazards?
questions.context: INCIDENT RECORD — An aggressive person is throwing objects near the entrance. Equipment partly blocks the nearest exit route.
answers: Keep clear, move others towards a safer route and alert appropriate help
Approach and argue until the person stops
Retrieve the equipment beside the person before leaving
Ask an untrained bystander to block the thrown objects

questions.question: What total distance belongs in the record?
questions.context: INCIDENT RECORD — One access route measures 0.4 km. A second section measures 250 m. Write the combined distance in metres.

questions.question: Which sentence is the clearest concise handover?
questions.context: HANDOVER DETAIL — At 10:20, breathing became faster and the person became newly confused. Both changes are new.
answers: Things changed at some point and there were several details
The room was quiet before something happened
At 10:20, breathing became faster and the person became newly confused
There are many normal details to discuss before the new changes

profiles.title: The Rapid-Response Natural

profiles.title: The Calm Scene Solver
profiles.copy: You handled a broad mix of body knowledge, scene decisions and multi-clue cases with steady reasoning. A few finer handover and observation details kept the entrance challenge interesting.

profiles.title: The Steady Responder
profiles.copy: You built a solid result by following visible evidence and treating safety seriously. Your strongest area shows where your emergency-learning instincts are already taking shape.

profiles.title: The Promising Candidate

profiles.title: The First-Response Explorer

details.tipsTitle: Three ways to sharpen your response thinking
details.tipsIntro: These are general quiz strategies—not clinical instruction, medical advice or a professional assessment.

tips.title: Scan for immediate danger
tips.copy: Before interpreting finer details, identify hazards, sudden deterioration and airway or breathing concerns.

tips.title: Compare with the baseline
tips.copy: A change from the earlier record can matter more than memorising one isolated number.

tips.title: Use every visible clue
tips.copy: Build the answer from the complete scene rather than letting one dramatic detail decide everything.

about.body:
This worldwide entertainment challenge explores entrance-level paramedic knowledge across 40 varied questions. It covers anatomy and physiology, emergency numeracy, observation trends, scene safety, calm communication, handover and multi-clue prioritisation.

The five challenges become progressively more applied, moving from accessible dispatch foundations into body systems, scene judgement, competing priorities and a final integrated response. Questions use worldwide principles rather than country-specific protocols or specialist treatment decisions.

Your final percentage reflects only the answers given in this entertainment quiz. It is a playful snapshot of the response areas that felt strongest and the topics that proved more challenging, not a judgement of clinical competence or suitability for paramedic practice.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Work through each response challenge at your own pace—there is no timer or speed bonus.
Choose the single option best supported by the visible clues. Correctness stays hidden until the final reveal.
Keep going as the decisions become harder, then reveal your score and complete answer review.
